observations: Photo 0: TV screen shows an Xbox dashboard with a gold/tan Xbox One X render as wallpaper, tile for 'FC26' visible, console body is black and covered in stickers, one black game controller sits in front.
Photo 1: Same black sticker-covered console, controller in front, TV shows a live football match (gameplay, team names MCI vs MUN).
Photo 2: TV shows 'EA SPORTS FC 26' loading screen; console again shown covered in stickers, same single controller visible.
No photo shows the rear ports, the underside label/serial, the storage/settings menu, a second controller, or the UK receipt.

The console's actual shape (flat, wide, single row of top vents) is consistent with an Xbox One X body, but the dashboard wallpaper is a generic Xbox render and not proof of the real hardware underneath the stickers.
Only one controller is visible in all three photos despite the seller writing 'pads' (plural).

identity.kind: Xbox game console (seller states Xbox One X / 'series 1x')
read_from: photo 0 dashboard wallpaper (ambiguous, not a label)

claims.evidence: No serial/label or settings 'About' screen shown in any photo; console body hidden under stickers.

claims.claim: 6 games installed (FC26, Far Cry 3, Modern Warfare 3, Dishonored 2, Tomb...)
claims.evidence: Only FC26 is shown running/loading in photos 1 and 2; the other 5 titles are not shown on screen or in a game library list.

claims.claim: Neatly used, never opened or repaired
claims.evidence: No photo of screws, seals, or internal casing.
No stress-test video or thermal evidence; a single short clip of gameplay in photo 1 does not prove sustained use.
Rear/side ports not shown in any photo.
Only one controller is visible in all three photos; no second pad shown.
No photo of the receipt provided.

risks.risk: Exact Xbox model (One X vs Series S/X) materially changes value and is not legible under the stickers.
risks.proof: Clear photo of the bottom label/serial sticker or the Settings > System > About screen showing model and storage.
risks.if_unproven: priced as the lowest-value plausible model (Xbox One X) rather than a newer Series console

risks.risk: Storage capacity (affects number of games it can truly hold) is unknown.
risks.proof: Screenshot of storage settings showing used/free space and total capacity.
risks.if_unproven: priced at base/lowest common capacity for that model

risks.risk: Second controller may not exist despite 'pads' claim.
risks.proof: Photo showing both controllers together, powered on.

risks.risk: Stickers may be hiding cracks, dents, or non-original shell/repair marks.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of edges/corners and a video of stickers being peeled back in one spot.
risks.if_unproven: priced as cosmetically unverified / assume moderate wear

risks.risk: Internal repair or part-swap history cannot be ruled out despite claim.
risks.proof: Photo of intact warranty-void screws/seals on the underside.

risks.risk: Overheating or port failure not demonstrated under load.
risks.proof: Short video of console running a demanding game for several minutes with fan noise audible, plus a photo of all rear ports connected.
risks.if_unproven: priced as not fully verified working (worst case: port/overheat issue present)

risks.risk: UK receipt authenticity and relevance (proves import origin/warranty, not condition) cannot be checked.
risks.proof: Clear photo of the receipt showing date, serial match, and retailer.
risks.if_unproven: priced as if no receipt provided

proof_requests: Photo of the console's bottom label/serial number or the Settings > System > About screen (model + storage).
Photo showing both controllers together, powered on.
Close-up photos of console edges/corners without obstruction by stickers.
Short video of the console running a demanding game for a few minutes (to check fan/overheating) with ports visible.
response.reason: The seller's claimed model ('series 1x') cannot be confirmed because the console body is fully covered in stickers and no label or settings screen is shown, and this model identity drives the price tier; a worst-case price cannot be set without at least seeing the model/storage proof.
